annotations.title: DPIA intake as a Word file

description: Use this when the user wants the DPIA intake of a concrete, intended use of AI or of personal data as a Word file to work on, and, where the FRIA comes into play, the FRIA draft too. It takes the same fixed fact answers as the case check of Praxikon, as coded choices, and gives the same documents as the download on the site: the four parts of Article 35(7) GDPR with the seventeen points of the Dutch government model DPIA, each point filled from the facts given, partly filled, or left as an open question, with articles and source links. Leave out what is not known: it counts as unknown and becomes an open question, never a no. Send only the coded answers and never the case text, names or other personal data; there is no field for them. The answer gives a download_url: the case check on the site with the answers in the part after #, which the browser never sends to the server; opening it shows the outcome and builds the Word file in the user's browser. Give the user that link, the explanation and the summary, and show the notice. Praxikon keeps no copy of the file.

inputSchema.description: The same coded answers, with the same codes and meanings, as the input of check_case. Leave out every answer that is not known.

lang.description: Language of the document. Dutch is the default.

store_for_improvement.description: Optional. Set to false when the user asks that Praxikon does not keep this request to improve its answers; nothing of this call is then kept beyond the anonymous daily count. See https://www.praxikon.com/nl/legal/privacy, section 2.7.

name: export_dpia_intake

download_url.description: The case check with the answers in the URL fragment; the browser builds the Word file.

summary.description: What the intake holds, point by point, as plain text to show in the chat.
